documents.title: Responsible AI Use at UCF: Ethical Guidelines
documents.stance_why: The page says "Students should look to individual syllabi for guidance on how, when, and if AI use is permitted" and that UCF has no AI-specific policy "as yet", so it sets no default for students beyond disclosure and integrity rules and hands the decision to instructors.
documents.summary: University-wide ethical guidelines from UCF's AI for All initiative. They require disclosure of intentional AI use, bar uploading copyrighted material, send students to individual syllabi, and add duties for faculty, researchers and staff. They also say no AI-specific university policy exists yet.

units.why: The sentence says AI use "must be disclosed" for any element of a work or school product; it binds everyone and is the disclosure duty, P24.
units.anchor: The intentional use of AI-assisted tools for any element of a work or school product
units.policy: The intentional use of AI-assisted tools for any element of a work or school product must be disclosed

units.why: The example disclosure names the tool, the protection mode and the date; I chose P25 over P24 because it shows what details a disclosure carries, while the duty itself is the previous unit.
units.anchor: an outline of topics for this work were generated by Copilot with Enterprise Data Protection,
units.policy: An example disclosure names the tool (Copilot with Enterprise Data Protection), what it generated and the date.
units.fit_note: Gives one example disclosure and does not require each detail.

units.why: "does not need to be disclosed" exempts AI embedded in software such as predictive text, auto-correct and spell check from the disclosure rule, which is P100.
units.anchor: Use of AI that is embedded within larger software (e.g., predictive text sentence completions, auto-correct,
units.frag_start: Use of AI that is embedded
units.frag_end: does not need to be disclosed.
units.policy: Use of AI that is embedded within larger software (e.g., predictive text sentence completions, auto-correct, spell check, etc.), does not need to be disclosed.

units.why: "not centrally mandated for students, but may depend on individual faculty policy" leaves grammar-assistance disclosure to instructors, so P04 fits.
units.anchor: Disclosing the use of grammar assistance is not centrally mandated for students, but may depend
units.policy: Disclosing the use of grammar assistance is not centrally mandated for students, but may depend on individual faculty policy.

units.why: Uploading copyrighted materials, including "student assignments, publisher materials," to a tool that trains on or stores them "is a copyright violation"; the operative rule is an upload ban on course and protected materials, so P49 over P52.
units.anchor: It is a copyright violation to upload intellectual property / copyrighted materials
units.fit_note: Applies to tools that train on or store inputs and is framed as a copyright matter.

units.why: "Most AI tools use queries, uploads, and outputs to help train and refine their models" is a fact that underlies privacy caution (AI tools store prompts), P50.
units.anchor: Most AI tools use queries, uploads, and outputs to help train and refine their models.

units.why: AI tools "may warrant extra attention" because of money needed and "energy requirements"; it names cost and environmental concerns, so P53 fits.
units.anchor: or the energy requirements of AI tools
units.policy: AI tools can create situations that may warrant extra attention, such as the resources or money needed for some advanced tools and their energy requirements.
units.fit_note: Also touches cost and resource access (P51) in the same sentence.

units.why: "deepfakes and hallucinations must be acknowledged and must not be used fraudulently" bans deceptive AI use, so P74 fits.
units.anchor: deepfakes and hallucinations must be acknowledged and must not be used fraudulently

units.why: "All people bear responsibility to vet content" makes everyone responsible for checking AI content and not passing on deepfakes; P31 (verify output) fits as the duty is to vet content.
units.anchor: All people bear responsibility to vet content and ensure their use does not generate, transmit,
units.policy: All people bear responsibility to vet content and ensure their use does not generate, transmit, or perpetuate deepfakes

units.why: The page says UCF has no AI-specific policy yet and points to a separate page of internal policies; it states the status of the institutional framework, so P56 is nearest, with a note that it says the framework does not yet exist.
units.anchor: There is not, as yet, a Policy specifically about artificial intelligence.
units.policy: The "AI for All" initiative maintains a separate page about internal policies that apply to technologies, including artificial intelligence; there is not, as yet, a Policy specifically about artificial intelligence.
units.fit_note: Describes the absence of an AI-specific university policy rather than stating principles.

units.why: "no statewide guidelines or mandates" and "Congress is considering, but has not yet passed" federal law describe the external legal environment; no law yet applies, so P77 is the nearest, with a note.
units.anchor: There are, as yet, no statewide guidelines or mandates for AI use or non-use.
units.frag_end: federal laws about AI use or non-use.
units.policy: There are, as yet, no statewide guidelines or mandates for AI use or non-use in Florida, and Congress is considering, but has not yet passed, federal laws about AI use or non-use.
units.fit_note: States that no external law yet applies rather than requiring compliance with one.

units.why: The FAA guidance bars use of GAI for illegal or malicious activity, as direct authority for decisions, to circumvent policy, or to infringe IP; UCF says stakeholders "are likely bound", so it is an external-rule compliance policy, P77.
units.anchor: UCF stakeholders are likely bound by these guidelines.
units.frag_start: As a contractor of the FAA, UCF
units.policy: As a contractor of the FAA, UCF stakeholders are likely bound by FAA guidance that personnel must not use GAI to perform or facilitate illegal or malicious activities, cite it as direct evidence or authority for a decision, circumvent applicable requirements, harm or imitate individuals or groups, or infringe the intellectual property of a third party.
units.fit_note: Conditional ("likely bound"), and the quoted rules are also deception and IP limits.

units.why: "Students should look to individual syllabi for guidance on how, when, and if AI use is permitted" leaves the rule to each syllabus, so P04 fits; the student duty to look is secondary.
units.anchor: Students should look to individual syllabi for guidance on how, when, and if AI use
units.policy: Students should look to individual syllabi for guidance on how, when, and if AI use is permitted.
units.fit_note: Also states that the rule is set per syllabus (P04).

units.why: "If no policy is stated, students should seek clarification from the instructor" is the ask-when-unsure rule, P10.
units.anchor: If no policy is stated, students should seek clarification from the instructor

units.why: "Students are responsible for the accuracy of the work they submit, whether AI assistance was employed or not" makes students answerable for submitted work, P29.
units.anchor: Students are responsible for the accuracy of the work they submit

units.why: "Students who fraudulently represent AI output as their work are committing plagiarism" classifies misrepresenting AI output as plagiarism, P36.
units.anchor: Students who fraudulently represent AI output as their work are committing plagiarism.

units.why: AI should complement creativity "but not a replacement for their own critical thinking", with AI as a "thought partner"; students stay the primary thinker, P32.
units.anchor: not a replacement for their own critical thinking
units.policy: AI should be considered as a way to complement students' creativity and intellectual capabilities, but not a replacement for their own critical thinking; AI is best positioned as a "thought partner" that challenges, extends and enhances student thinking rather than substituting for it.

units.why: The passage says assignments develop "the PROCESS of intellectual growth" and the journey "cannot be skipped"; it gives the skill-building reason for limits, P41.
units.anchor: cannot be skipped without compromising the learning objectives
units.frag_end: these experiences are designed to cultivate.

units.why: "faculty must ensure their use of AI for teaching is ethical, responsible, fair, transparent, and disclosed" sets a faculty duty including disclosure; P47 is nearest.
units.anchor: their use of AI for teaching is ethical, responsible, fair, transparent, and disclosed
units.fit_note: Also sets general ethical conduct duties, not only disclosure to students.

units.why: "Grading accomplished only through AI, with no human review, is not ethical and should be avoided" requires a human in grading, P46.
units.anchor: Grading accomplished only through AI, with no human review, is not ethical and should be
units.policy: Grading accomplished only through AI, with no human review, is not ethical and should be avoided.

units.why: "Faculty are advised to avoid using AI detectors. They are not reliable" advises against detectors because of false positives and negatives, P39.
units.anchor: Faculty are advised to avoid using AI detectors. They are not reliable

units.why: Research that non-native writers are "disproportionately likely to be unjustly accused of AI use" names a bias harm of detection; I chose P53 over P39 because P39 is the previous unit and this adds the equity harm.
units.anchor: students writing in a non-native language are disproportionately likely to be unjustly accused of AI
units.policy: students writing in a non-native language are disproportionately likely to be unjustly accused of AI use
units.fit_note: Names bias in detection against non-native writers.

units.why: "faculty may want to consider assignments that encourage student AI use as part of the learning process" suggests redesigning assignments around AI, P35.
units.anchor: faculty may want to consider assignments that encourage student AI use as part of the
units.policy: faculty may want to consider assignments that encourage student AI use as part of the learning process

units.why: "Recommendation letters produced solely by AI lack the personal insights" cautions against solely AI-written letters in faculty work, an instructor teaching-work use, P59.
units.anchor: Recommendation letters produced solely by AI lack the personal insights and specific details
units.frag_start: Recommendation letters produced solely by AI
units.fit_note: Stated as an observation about credibility rather than an explicit ban.

units.why: "Faculty should check with individual publishers regarding policies of AI use and/or disclosure" defers publication AI rules to the venue, as P62 describes.
units.anchor: Faculty should check with individual publishers regarding policies of AI use and/or disclosure.

units.why: Grant-writing AI use "is not universally accepted" and "faculty will need to make case-by-case decisions"; this is a research-use rule, P62.
units.anchor: the use of AI tools for grant-writing is not universally accepted, and faculty will need
units.policy: the use of AI tools for grant-writing is not universally accepted, and faculty will need to make case-by-case decisions
units.fit_note: Leaves the decision case by case and does not defer to funder rules in this sentence.

units.why: "Some grant and publication organizations prohibit the use of AI when writing critiques, reviews" and faculty "should seek clarification" case by case; a venue deferral for peer review, P62.
units.anchor: Faculty should seek clarification about whether AI tools are permitted on a case-by-case basis.

units.why: Research data analysis "only via enterprise-level platform access to ensure data integrity and data security" limits AI to vetted platforms; I chose P50 over P62 because the concern is data protection.
units.anchor: only via enterprise-level platform access to ensure data integrity and data security
units.frag_start: Researchers are responsible for the protection

units.why: "For scholarly reviews, researchers should avoid using AI. Human expertise and judgment remain essential" sets a review-specific limit in research, P62.
units.anchor: For scholarly reviews, researchers should avoid using AI.

units.why: "staff and administrators must ensure their use of AI is ethical, responsible, fair, transparent, and disclosed" is a general conduct duty for staff AI use in operations, P76.
units.anchor: UCF staff and administrators must ensure their use of AI is ethical, responsible, fair, transparent,
units.frag_start: Like all UCF stakeholders, UCF staff
units.policy: UCF staff and administrators must ensure their use of AI is ethical, responsible, fair, transparent, and disclosed.

units.why: Staff "must be extra vigilant not to expose proprietary data, student records, and other sensitive information to unsecured AI" is a data protection duty, P50.
units.anchor: must be extra vigilant not to expose proprietary data, student records, and other sensitive information
units.policy: must be extra vigilant not to expose proprietary data, student records, and other sensitive information to unsecured AI

units.why: "De-identifying data is always preferred before exposing it to AI, even within the protections afforded with Copilot" adds a data-minimization practice, P50.
units.anchor: De-identifying data is always preferred before exposing it to AI

units.why: The acknowledgments say the principles were "developed and written without AI assistance" and name the groups consulted, describing how the guidance was made, P84.
units.anchor: The Responsible Use principles above were developed and written without AI assistance.
units.policy: The Responsible Use principles were developed and written without AI assistance; groups that assisted in fine-tuning them include UCF IT, UCF Libraries, UCF Center for Ethics, Center for Distributed Learning, Faculty Center for Teaching & Learning, Faculty Senate IT Committee, Office of Research, and several groups and coordinators exploring AI at departmental or College levels.

documents.title: Ethical Use of AI (students)
documents.stance_why: The page says to consult the syllabus and ask the instructor if none is stated, and that AI "should be avoided unless explicitly permitted by the instructor", while also saying "Students must embrace the inevitable changes"; it sets no single rule and leaves the decision to instructors.
documents.summary: Student-facing guidance that recommends UCF's licensed Copilot, tells students to follow each syllabus, verify AI output and own its errors, and explains the learning cost of cognitive offloading. It also argues that AI fluency matters for careers and suggests keeping an AI portfolio.

units.why: The page says "Students must embrace the inevitable changes, and, moreover, become proficient users of AI to remain competitive"; an expectation grounded in professional skill, P44.
units.anchor: Students must embrace the inevitable changes, and, moreover, become proficient users of AI
units.frag_end: to remain competitive in the workplace.

units.why: The quoted line "the person who knows how to use AI will replace you" is a career-pressure argument for learning AI, P44.
units.anchor: the person who knows how to use AI will replace you
units.frag_start: “AI is not going to replace you.
units.policy: The page quotes: "AI is not going to replace you. But the person who knows how to use AI will replace you."
units.fit_note: A quoted slogan, not a rule.

units.why: "The official AI tool at UCF is Copilot-Chat" under a "Recommended AI Tool" heading; an institution-wide sanctioned tool, so P92 rather than P17 (course-specific).
units.anchor: The official AI tool at UCF is Copilot-Chat
units.frag_start: The official AI tool at UCF
units.fit_note: Labeled "Recommended"; the page does not say other tools are banned.

units.why: Copilot with Commercial Protection is a "walled garden" where inputs "are NOT added to the system's memory, database, or future answers"; this explains why the vetted tool protects data, P50.
units.anchor: Inputs into Copilot with Commercial Protection are NOT added to the system’s memory, database, or
units.frag_start: Data stays local and is NOT uploaded
units.policy: Inputs into Copilot with Commercial Protection are NOT added to the system’s memory, database, or future answers.

units.why: The page says a local copy is kept in a hidden mailbox "per UCF retention policies"; this discloses that the tool retains prompts, P50.
units.anchor: a local copy is kept in a hidden (local) mailbox folder in your own Sharepoint
units.policy: a local copy is kept in a hidden (local) mailbox folder in your own Sharepoint account

units.why: The login steps and the "green shield" check tell students how to reach the data-protection mode of the sanctioned tool; practical guidance on using the approved tool, P92.
units.anchor: The safe version of UCF’s Copilot is accessed via this procedure
units.policy: The safe version of UCF's Copilot is accessed by signing in at portal.office.com with the UCF email and NID as a "work or school" account; a checkmark in a green shield indicates "data protection" mode.
units.fit_note: Procedural instructions for accessing the tool.

units.why: "Before using AI to complete an assignment, consult the syllabus" tells students to find the course rule first, P78.
units.anchor: Before using AI to complete an assignment, consult the syllabus.

units.why: "If there is no stated policy on AI usage, ask the instructor" is the ask-when-unsure rule, P10.
units.anchor: If there is no stated policy on AI usage, ask the instructor for guidelines

units.why: "AI-generated content is unreliable. It may be invented, biased, inaccurate" and "carefully evaluating the output is essential" is the verify-output rule, P31.
units.anchor: carefully evaluating the output is essential
units.frag_start: If AI tools are permitted, be aware

units.why: "the completed work is the student's responsibility and AI errors are considered student errors" makes students own AI mistakes, P29.
units.anchor: AI errors are considered student errors

units.why: "its use should be avoided unless explicitly permitted by the instructor" sets what applies when no permission is given, so P06 (fallback rule) fits; it is worded as advice ("should be avoided"), hence restrict, not P01.
units.anchor: its use should be avoided unless explicitly permitted by the instructor
units.frag_start: While AI may offer a tempting shortcut
units.fit_note: Worded as advice ("should be avoided") and attached to coursework generally.

units.why: The forklift-at-the-gym analogy and "The struggle is the point" explain that AI shortcuts the practice that builds skill, P41.
units.anchor: The struggle is the point. Only through effort and challenge can growth occur.

units.why: Relying on AI "undermines long-term learning" and "There are no shortcuts to attaining these skills" restate the skill-building rationale; P41 because it is about practice, not novices.
units.anchor: Relying on AI to bypass that process may result in short-term gains, but it undermines
units.policy: Relying on AI to bypass that process may result in short-term gains, but it undermines long-term learning

units.why: "developing AI fluency is essential... those who can use AI tools effectively stand out during the interview process" is a career-skill argument, P44.
units.anchor: developing AI fluency is essential
units.frag_start: That said, developing AI fluency is essential.
units.policy: Developing AI fluency is essential; in today's workplace, those who can use AI tools effectively stand out during the interview process and in the workforce.

units.why: "AI is a tool. Let it assist you, not replace you" keeps students as the primary problem-solver, P32.
units.anchor: AI is a tool. Let it assist you, not replace you.

units.why: "consider creating and maintaining an AI Portfolio" asks students to keep a record of their AI uses to show employers; no type covers a voluntary career portfolio (P26 is a submission duty), so UNCOVERED.
units.anchor: consider creating and maintaining an
units.frag_start: To showcase these skills and other ways
units.uncovered_note: Students are advised to keep an AI Portfolio documenting their AI use in coursework to show employers.

units.why: "One of the best ways to position yourself as an AI-fluent job candidate is to prepare by using a broad range of AI tools" advises using many tools for careers, P44.
units.anchor: prepare by using a broad range of AI tools and becoming aware of their differences
units.frag_start: One of the best ways to position yourself

notes: Both documents are university-layer AI for All web pages with no tiers. No school or computing-unit documents were collected. One UNCOVERED unit: the AI Portfolio suggestion.
